reformulation: Agent finding -> kernel certificate for an exact singleton reformulation of a 200-variable / 100-row integer MPS (560 nonzeros; 100 binary x carrying the whole objective, 100 general-integer y): 100 mod-2 row-combination certificates force every binary (37 ones, 63 zeros), each equality then fixes its own auxiliary, so the source feasible set is one point with objective 37; the target is a single continuous coordinate pinned by the equality objective_value = 37. Two mutually inverse directional claims (objective Equal, projection [], inverse 1/0), 805 obligations, RPA 2,238,283 B -> RPX 400,516 B, request 308 B, 14 turns / 0 failures / 291.8 s.
claim_class: Feasible-set singleton bijection between two explicit models, stated as two directional claims that are each other's inverse: claim 0 reverse=false, input_integers and output_integers true, objective Equal, projection [], inverse=1, forward map = the constant 37; claim 1 reverse=true, same flags, inverse=0, map = all 200 proved source values. No points, bijections or improvements records; LP equality is not requested.
claims: claim 0 (forward, integer domain): 203 obligations = 1 target bound + 1 target row + 1 objective equality + 200 inverse-identity equations; only 2 of them are literal Exact, the other 201 are Lin steps, and block 0 carries 838 steps.

claim 1 (reverse, integer domain): 602 obligations = 100 x (lower+upper+Int) + 100 y (lower+Int) + 100 source rows + 1 objective + 1 forward-map identity, of which 600 are Exact constants; block 1 has 2 steps because its map is a constant vector.

kernel verify (debug): obligations 805, linear_terms 35159, peak_live_facts 838, branches 0, work 108015, execute 172176 us; assemble 79214 us -> 400516 B RPX (cases/test84/preparation.json kernel_runs).
Source uniqueness is not a claim field: it exists only as the 100 parity chains plus 100 equality fixings inside block 0, i.e. proved unique rather than merely exhibited (cases/test84/README.md).

proof_encoding: RPA 2 text built with json.dumps(cert,indent=2) at prepare_test84.py:95: 2,238,283 B = a two-record claims array plus block 0 (838 steps) and block 1 (2 steps), i.e. 5.6x the 400,516 B RPX.
Block 0 decomposes as 537 parity-chain steps (63 five-step chains for x=0, 37 six-step chains for x=1), 100 one-step equality fixings and 201 Lin steps for the non-trivial forward obligations.

Each parity chain is Lin Int over half the selected equality sum plus integer VarInt multiples, then a branch-specific finish: for v=0 a VarUpper Le, Round, doubling Le and EqPair with VarLower; for v=1 a negated Int, VarLower Le, Round, Le and EqPair with VarUpper.
The equality fixings are one Lin Eq per remaining coordinate, from its own row scaled by 1/pivot with the proved terms subtracted (prepare_test84.py:55-61); no solver or numerical solve is used.

35,159 linear terms in total for a one-variable target; the claims array is written twice (request.json and inside proof.rpa) and each of the two mutations is a full 2.2 MB copy re-assembled to 400,515 / 400,517 B.
agent_manual_work: Wrote two independent MPS readers (eval 'Parsing exact model and validating domains', plus a regex read_mps inside the generated output/verify.py) and pinned the semantics by hand: LI overrides the INTORG binary default, an absent RHS is zero, no RANGES/OBJSENSE.
Ran GF(2) Gauss-Jordan itself on bitmask rows of the augmented [A | I]: rank 100, nullity 0, 100 row-combination certificates (eval 'Computing exact modular row certificates').

Re-verified each certificate by integer summation of the original coefficient dictionaries: odd coefficient on the named x, even elsewhere, forced value = combined RHS mod 2 (eval 'Verifying singleton feasibility and objective').
Solved the auxiliaries exactly (y_r = (sum of x over S_r - b_r)/2 -> 15 zeros, 68 ones, 17 twos) and checked all 100 equalities, 200 bounds, 200 integrality conditions and objective 37.

Rejected three hypotheses by hand: 100 individually-necessary row witnesses, incidence connectedness (300 nodes, one component) and the integrality-relaxation counterexample (all x=1, 61 fractional y, example y#2#2 = 5/2); the resulting 206 KB audit.json is the preparer's input.

friction: 2,238,283 B of pretty-printed RPA (indent=2) for 838 steps and 35,159 linear terms against a 1-variable target; the same text is written again for each mutation and re-assembled at 79,214 us per run.
The reverse block is 2 steps and 602 literal obligation refs: all of its bytes are the source model restated, although the list is fully determined by the two actual models.
The finding reaches the proof as an untyped audit.json (206 KB) read by string keys: audit['modular_certificates'] and audit['original_unique_assignment'] (prepare_test84.py:25,63).
Round is the only step whose derived fact must be recomputed by the caller, which is why the helper is copied into 11 files instead of shared.
The retained INVALID receipts carry free text only ('obligation 3'), no claim/block/step, so locating a rejected step inside an 838-step block means bisecting.
